findings.message: P1 upstream restatement: task T001 goes beyond target + operation + anchors by restating the upstream scanner contract, including live-surface roots, retired identifier/path checks, M-token state-expression checks, fail-closed I/O behavior, and specific positive/negative test behaviors. `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` requires task text to use target + operation + anchor cite instead.

P1 upstream restatement: task T002 restates upstream behavior via `without changing the other verify methods`, `success, verifier-finding failure`, and `fail-closed error propagation`. Keep this as target + operation + anchor cite under `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

P1 upstream restatement: task T003 restates verifier behavior with `expose it in sotp verify help`, `clean outcome rendering`, and `non-zero verifier outcome rendering` instead of relying on the cited AC/CN anchors. This violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

P1 upstream restatement: task T004 repeats upstream distribution-boundary behavior (`leave overlay Makefile unconnected`, no boundary-manifest exclude or runtime opt-out, maintainer CI includes the gate while exported-template CI does not). Per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, the task should cite the relevant anchors instead of restating the contract.

P1 upstream restatement: section S1 repeats scanner semantics, live-surface traversal, fail-closed I/O handling, and positive/negative test behavior. Plan sections are covered by `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` and should stay to ordering rationale plus anchors.

P1 upstream restatement: section S2 repeats the secondary-port behavior and existing error-propagation shape. `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md` allows target + operation + anchor cite, not prose restatement of the contract.

P1 upstream restatement: section S3 repeats CLI-driver input, clap subcommand, composition dispatch, and route/rendering behavior already owned by the spec/type anchors. This should be reduced to ordering plus anchor cites under `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

P1 upstream restatement: section S4 repeats the maintainer-only CI/export boundary contract, including overlay remaining unconnected and no manifest excludes or runtime switches. That is upstream behavior restatement forbidden by `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

T003 does not name all targets needed for its own CLI routing/test operation. The branch adds the new `VerifyCommand::RetentionGate` arm in `apps/cli/src/main.rs::verify_command_gate_name` and CLI coverage in `apps/cli/src/commands/verify_tests.rs`, but the task only lists `apps/cli-driver/src/verify.rs`, `apps/cli/src/commands/verify.rs`, and `apps/cli-composition/src/verify.rs`. An executor following this task would have to discover those additional CLI entrypoint/test targets outside the plan, so the task description is not fully executable under the impl-plan policy.

T002 cites AC-10 as part of its executable anchor set, and the summary repeats that T002 carries AC-10, but task-coverage maps AC-10 only to T001/T004. This leaves the impl-plan and coverage SSoT disagreeing about whether T002 is responsible for the CI-level acceptance criterion, so traceability for T002 is not sound until AC-10 is either removed from T002 or added to coverage with a plausible validation step.

T003 cites AC-10 as part of its executable anchor set, and the summary repeats that T003 carries AC-10, but task-coverage maps AC-10 only to T001/T004. This makes the CLI-routing task appear responsible for the CI-level acceptance criterion in impl-plan while the coverage artifact says it is not, leaving inconsistent task traceability.

`infrastructure::verify::retention_gate::verify` restates upstream behavior in its `docs` field: live-surface scanning, retired identifier/path detection, M-token state-expression handling, and scanner I/O fail-closed/no-panic behavior are already owned by IN-03/IN-04/IN-05/CN-01. Per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, catalogue docs should identify the changed symbol and cite anchors rather than reproduce the behavior contract.

The `FsVerifyAdapter -> usecase::verify::VerifyPort` trait impl is declared `action: reference`, but this track requires that existing impl to gain the retention-gate delegation for the newly added `verify_retention_gate` port method. `reference` is for baseline entries the track does not modify, so this hides an adapter-side contract change that should be declared as a modified impl entry.

The `VerifyInteractor -> VerifyService` trait impl is declared `action: reference`, while `VerifyService` is modified to add `verify_retention_gate`; the existing interactor impl must add the corresponding delegation method. Keeping the impl as `reference` declares it unchanged and leaves the service-side implementation change outside the type contract.

`walk()` accepts symlinked descendants under `LIVE_SURFACE`: `std::fs::metadata()` and `read_dir()` will follow a symlinked `libs/`, `.claude/*`, etc., so a repo can redirect the scan outside the workspace. The adapter only rejects a symlinked root; this boundary needs the same `symlink_metadata()`/reject pattern used by `track::symlink_guard::reject_symlinks_below` and the `scope_config_loader.rs` symlink tests.

The retention scanner reads each live-surface file into memory with `std::fs::read` while recursively walking broad roots such as `libs` and `apps`. A large or generated file under those roots can make `sotp verify retention-gate` allocate unbounded memory and abort before it can return a fail-closed `VerifyFinding`. The infrastructure policy treats unbounded I/O paths as correctness findings; stream the file with a bounded reader or reject files over an explicit size limit with an error finding.

`test_verify_command_gate_name_uses_verify_prefix` does not exercise the newly added `VerifyCommand::RetentionGate` branch, so the new `verify-retention-gate` telemetry label is effectively untested. A typo in that label would still pass this test because the subcommand list only covers `latest-track`, `arch-docs`, and `layers`.

IN-03 says the live surface must be equivalent to the current gate, but then only requires scanning “at least” the listed roots. That leaves room to add more roots, while OS-04 explicitly declares live-surface expansion out of scope. Downstream implementers could satisfy IN-03 while violating OS-04, so the spec has a scope contradiction around scan semantics.

GO-01 requires the retention gate to run through the established verify chain, including infrastructure checker, usecase port/service, CLI driver input, CLI subcommand, and composition wiring. The acceptance criteria only prove the old integration test is gone and that a CLI help/execution path exists; a direct CLI shortcut could satisfy AC-01/AC-02 while bypassing the required architecture. This leaves GO-01 without deterministic AC coverage for the stated verify-chain contract.
findings.category: missing AC coverage for a stated goal

findings.message: GO-02 promises preservation of the live-surface scan semantics, and IN-03 lists the roots that define that surface, but no acceptance criterion proves the verifier actually scans each listed root. AC-03/AC-10 only require injection into one file under “the live surface,” so an implementation could omit roots such as `.claude/commands/**` or `.harness/capabilities/**` and still satisfy the AC text.
